frame: Roblox rig axes: +X right, +Y up, -Z front, feet at y = 0, centred on x = 0, z = 0 (studs). Blender authoring: (bx, by, bz) = (x, -z, y); FBX exported Y up / -Z forward, 1 unit = 1 stud.

looks.rule: Templates in `assemblies` are resolved exactly like Kit/CharacterMesh.luau (blender/lib/ckit_resolve.py is the Python port): %look.<axis>% picks one of the numbered variants (prefix + digits + suffix, numeric order) by the look (skin / hair / hairColor / outfit follow the field and spill over extra variants; face / boots / acc mix the look), %kingdom% is crimson | azure | emerald | gold. Variants: head_01..06 faces, hair_01..10 (10 = a kingdom hood) and hair_beard, torso_01..06 cuts, boot_01..03_l/_r, acc_01 (none) / acc_02 (headband).

tints.rule: MeshPart.Color = skin | hair | shade(kingdomColor, tint_factor) | cloth | white (fixed); baked vertex colours are multiplied by it. Unverified in Studio. The Blender renders use the values below, which mirror Kit/Character.luau.
tints.tint_shift_rule: soldier sleeves only: factor + tint_shift[(look.hairColor + look.skin - 2) % 8], clamped to 0.5..1 (an approximation of the runtime's per-individual shift)
tints.cloth_rule: cloth piece colour = (slot 'leg' ? cloth_legs : cloth_panels)[job or 'folk'][(look.hairColor - 1) % 3] x dye[look.hairColor - 1]
